# Nitrox: Complete AI Framework Manual & API Reference

> Generated for LLMs, AI agents, and developers building high-performance web applications with Nitrox.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

Nitrox is a minimalist, high-performance web framework for Rust inspired by the developer ergonomics of Express.js. It is built directly on Hyper 1.x and Tokio.

Key architectural pillars:
- **Zero-Clone State:** Inject shared state (DB pools, caches) into `Nitrox::with_state(state)` and access it anywhere via `req.state` with zero runtime locking and zero closure captures.
- **Express-Style Router Modularization:** Mount sub-routers via `app.mount("/prefix", router)` or `app.use_router("/prefix", router)`.
- **4-Tier Middleware Composition:** Global (`app.use_middleware`), Router-level (`router.use_middleware`), Route-level (`router.get_with`), and Fluent RouteBuilder (`router.route(path)`).
- **Zero-Cost Boot-Time Pre-Composition:** Middlewares are composed into a unified `HandlerFn` during route registration at startup, avoiding runtime lock contention and dynamic allocations.
- **Benchmark Performance:** Peak throughput of 130,000 to 186,000+ requests per second under high concurrency.

---

## 2. Complete API Specification

### Application (`Nitrox<S>`)
```rust
pub struct Nitrox<S = ()>;

impl Nitrox<()> {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
}

impl<S: Send + Sync + 'static> Nitrox<S> {
    pub fn with_state(state: S) -> Self;
    pub fn use_middleware<F, Fut>(&self, middleware: F) -> &Self;
    pub fn use_router(&self, path: &str, router: Router<S>) -> &Self;
    pub fn mount(&self, path: &str, router: Router<S>) -> &Self; // Alias for use_router
    
    // HTTP route registration
    pub fn get<F, Fut>(&self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &Self;
    pub fn post<F, Fut>(&self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &Self;
    pub fn put<F, Fut>(&self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &Self;
    pub fn delete<F, Fut>(&self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &Self;
    pub fn patch<F, Fut>(&self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &Self;

    // Route-level middleware registration
    pub fn get_with<M, H, Fut>(&self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn post_with<M, H, Fut>(&self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn put_with<M, H, Fut>(&self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn delete_with<M, H, Fut>(&self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn patch_with<M, H, Fut>(&self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;

    pub fn static_files(&self, route_path: &str, dir_path: &str) -> &Self;
    pub async fn listen(self, port: u16) -> Result<()>;
}
```

### Router (`Router<S>`)
```rust
pub struct Router<S = ()>;

impl Router<()> {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
}

impl<S: Send + Sync + 'static> Router<S> {
    pub fn with_state() -> Self;
    pub fn use_middleware<M, Fut>(&mut self, middleware: M) -> &mut Self;
    pub fn r#use<M, Fut>(&mut self, middleware: M) -> &mut Self; // Alias for use_middleware

    pub fn get<F, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &mut Self;
    pub fn post<F, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &mut Self;
    pub fn put<F, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &mut Self;
    pub fn delete<F, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &mut Self;
    pub fn patch<F, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, handler: F) -> &mut Self;

    pub fn get_with<M, H, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &mut Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn post_with<M, H, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &mut Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn put_with<M, H, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &mut Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn delete_with<M, H, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &mut Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;
    pub fn patch_with<M, H, Fut>(&mut self, path: &str, middlewares: M, handler: H) -> &mut Self where M: IntoMiddlewareChain<S>;

    pub fn route<'a>(&'a mut self, path: &'a str) -> RouteBuilder<'a, S>;
    pub fn mount(&mut self, prefix: &str, router: Router<S>) -> &mut Self;
}
```

### Request (`Request<S>`)
```rust
pub struct Request<S = ()> {
    pub state: Arc<S>,
    // ...
}

impl<S> Request<S> {
    pub fn method(&self) -> &Method;
    pub fn path(&self) -> &str;
    pub fn param(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str>;
    pub fn params(&self) -> &HashMap<String, String>;
    pub fn query(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str>;
    pub fn queries(&self) -> &HashMap<String, String>;
    pub fn header(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&str>;
    pub fn headers(&self) -> &HashMap<String, String>;
    pub fn bearer_token(&self) -> Option<&str>;
    pub fn content_type(&self) -> Option<&str>;
    pub async fn json<T: DeserializeOwned>(&mut self) -> Result<T>;
    pub async fn body_string(&mut self) -> Result<String>;
    pub async fn body_bytes(&mut self) -> Result<Bytes>;
    pub fn state(&self) -> &S;
}
```

### Response Builder
```rust
pub struct Response;

impl Response {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub fn status(self, code: u16) -> Self;
    pub fn header(self, key: &str, value: &str) -> Self;
    pub fn send(self, body: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn send_bytes(self, bytes: impl Into<Bytes>) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn html(self, body: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn json<T: Serialize>(self, data: T) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn cookie(self, name: &str, value: &str, options: CookieOptions) -> Self;
    pub fn redirect(self, location: &str) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn cors(self, origin: &str) -> Self;
}
```

---

## 3. Middleware Architecture & Execution Lifecycle

### Lifecycle Flow
1. **Global Middlewares:** Run in FIFO order.
2. **Router Middlewares:** Run in FIFO order for routes mounted under this router.
3. **Route Middlewares:** Run in FIFO order for this specific route.
4. **Terminal Handler:** Generates HTTP Response.
5. **Unwind (Reverse LIFO):** Response passes back through route middlewares, router middlewares, and global middlewares.

### Multiple Middlewares via Tuples
`IntoMiddlewareChain<S>` is implemented for:
- Single middleware: `mw`
- Tuples of 2 to 8: `(mw1, mw2)`, `(mw1, mw2, mw3)`, etc.
- Vector: `vec![mw1, mw2]`

Example:
```rust
router.get_with("/protected", (require_auth, require_admin, audit_log), |req, res| async move {
    res.json(serde_json::json!({"status": "ok"}))
});
```

### Short-Circuiting Guarantee
If a middleware returns a `Response` without calling `next(req, res).await`, all downstream middlewares and the terminal handler are bypassed immediately.

---

## 4. Critical Rust Gotchas for Developers and AI Agents

### Gotcha A: The `.to_string()` vs `.as_str()` JSON Trap
When parsing untyped JSON (`serde_json::Value`):
- `val["username"].to_string()` produces `"\"alice\""` (WITH LITERAL QUOTES).
- Searching SQL or MongoDB with `"\"alice\""` fails completely!
- **CORRECT FIX:** Always use `val["username"].as_str()`, which returns `Option<&str>` (`Some("alice")` without quotes).
- **BEST PRACTICE:** Use strongly typed structs with `#[derive(Deserialize)]` instead of `Value`.

### Gotcha B: Database Connection Pools and the Mutex Trap
- Connection pools (`sqlx::PgPool`, `mongodb::Database`, `redis::aio::ConnectionManager`) are ALREADY thread-safe smart pointers internally.
- **NEVER** wrap them in an outer `Mutex` (e.g. `Arc<Mutex<PgPool>>`). Doing so forces the server to process all database queries serially, destroying concurrency.
- Store them directly in your `AppState` struct. Nitrox wraps `state` in an internal `Arc<S>` automatically, so `AppState` does NOT need manual `Arc` wrapping or `#[derive(Clone)]`.

### Gotcha C: Danger of `.unwrap()` in Production Handlers
- If a header, query param, or JSON field is missing, `.unwrap()` panics and crashes the worker task.
- Use safe alternatives:
  - `req.param("id").unwrap_or("default")`
  - `let Some(id) = req.param("id") else { return res.status(400).send("Missing ID"); };`

### Gotcha D: Modern `let else` Syntax
Prefer `let else` over nested `match` statements:
```rust
let Some(token) = req.bearer_token() else {
    return res.status(401).json(serde_json::json!({"error": "Missing token"}));
};
```

### Gotcha E: Zero Closure-Cloning with `with_state`
- DO NOT manually write `let db_clone = db.clone()` before routes or double-closures.
- Always initialize your app with `Nitrox::with_state(state)` and access `req.state.my_field` directly in any route or middleware.

---

## 5. Production Reference Template

```rust
use nitrox::prelude::*;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

// Plain struct: NO Arc wrapping, NO #[derive(Clone)] needed!
pub struct AppState {
    pub db_pool: sqlx::PgPool,
    pub redis: redis::aio::ConnectionManager,
}

#[derive(Deserialize)]
pub struct CreateUserDto {
    pub username: String,
    pub email: String,
}

pub async fn require_auth(
    req: Request<AppState>,
    res: Response,
    next: Next<AppState>,
) -> Response {
    let Some(token) = req.bearer_token() else {
        return res.status(401).json(serde_json::json!({
            "error": "Unauthorized: Bearer token required"
        }));
    };

    if token != "valid-token" {
        return res.status(401).json(serde_json::json!({
            "error": "Unauthorized: Invalid token"
        }));
    }

    next(req, res).await
}

pub fn create_user_router() -> Router<AppState> {
    let mut router = Router::with_state();

    router.use_middleware(nitrox::middleware::logger());

    router.get_with("/me", require_auth, |req, res| async move {
        res.json(serde_json::json!({ "user": "current_authenticated_user" }))
    });

    router.post_with("/", require_auth, |mut req, res| async move {
        let payload: CreateUserDto = req.json().await?;
        res.status(201).json(serde_json::json!({ "created": payload.username }))
    });

    router
}

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // Initialize DB and Redis here...
    // let state = AppState { db_pool, redis };
    // let mut app = Nitrox::with_state(state);
    // app.use_middleware(nitrox::middleware::helmet());
    // app.mount("/api/v1/users", create_user_router());
    // app.listen(3000).await?;
    Ok(())
}
```
